articleTitle: High-Power Submillimeter Wave Solid-State Sources
abstract: The development and measurements of solid-state active multiplier sources for DNP-NMR experiments is described in this paper. The sources utilize power-combined Schottky diode frequency doublers as the final two stages. 250 mW output power was measured for two complete sources, one at 250 GHz and a second at 262 GHz. Using a 1.3 mm probe, DNP enhancements of 115-120 were measured.

articleTitle: 28GHz Active Phased Array Antenna Employing GaAs Frontend Module for Massive MIMO in 5G
abstract: In 5G mobile communication systems, superb performances, namely large system capacity, low latency and massive connection are expected. A massive multiple input multiple output (MIMO)antenna has attracted a great attraction to become a key technology to meet such 5G requirements. In this paper, we report development results of an active phased array antenna (APAA)employing a highly integrated GaAs RF frontend module at 28 GHz-band. The transmission trial of 16-beam spatial-multiplexing using the APAA with 256 antenna elements is also reported. A spectral efficiency of 63.7 bps/Hz and a downlink transmission rate of 25.5 Gbps were successfully achieved.

articleTitle: Object and Direction Classification based on Range-Doppler Map of 79 GHz MIMO Radar Using a Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: We propose a convolutional neural network (CNN)which classifies the type and direction of a stationary object from the range-Doppler map acquired by a 79 GHz MIMO radar. The multi-class (21 classes)classification is performed by inputting the single frame range-Doppler map. We measured five kinds of objects oriented in four directions with the MIMO radar equipped with 32 virtual arrays of 4 TX and 8 RX from a distance of 5 m. The CNN with a small number of layers are proposed and range-Doppler maps of the selected virtual arrays are used for input. In the classification of 21 classes, the two convolution layer CNN achieves an accuracy of 92.2% by inputting four virtual arrays in the diagonal direction.

articleTitle: Analysis of Substrate Mounted Dielectric Lenses for Silicon-based THz Sources
abstract: In this paper, an analysis of on-chip integrated dipole antennas with silicon lenses is performed. Although the analysis is presented at 600GHz, the results can easily be extended to other antenna topologies and frequencies in the THz range. Both hemispherical and hyperhemispherical lenses are compared with a lens-less case. It is found that the use of a dielectric lens can prevent reflections at the bottom substrate interface and increase performance metrics such as gain and on-chip interelement coupling, as well as increase drastically the robustness of the design to antenna position. In the case of a hemispherical lens an optimum radius can be found for maximum directivity, while for hemispherical lenses the gain scales continuously with increasing lens radius as long as the shape is adjusted accordingly. The maximum simulated gain in the lens-less case is 1.8 dB while for the hemispherical case is 17.62 dB and for the hyperhemispherical it is 22.4 dB.

articleTitle: Divide-by-4 Injection-Locked Frequency Divider (ILFD) Using Stacked 2:1 ILFDs
abstract: A novel divide-by-4 injection-locked frequency divider (ILFD)is proposed and was implemented in the TSMC 0.18 μm 1P6M CMOS process. Conventional harmonic mixer divide-by-4 ILFD has limited locking range, and this letter shows a wide locking range divide-by-4 LC ILFD designed with one linear mixer divide-by-2 ILFD stacked on the top of the other linear mixer divide-by-2 ILFD. At the drain-source bias of 1.6V and at the incident power of 0 dBm, the locking range is 5.7 GHz (42.8%)from 11.4 to 17.1GHz at the power consumption of 9.93mW. The free-running oscillation frequency is 2.6GHz. The die area is 0.644 ×0.908mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

Author Keywords: divide-by-2 and divide-by-4 injection-locked frequency dividers

articleTitle: A 300GHz Dielectric Lens Antenna
abstract: In this paper, a 300GHz dielectric lens antenna made of PTFE (Teflon)material is introduced. The antenna is designed to be used in combination with an on-chip antenna which is possible to realize regarding the very short wavelength of the electromagnetic wave at 300GHz frequency. Using this combination in wireless transceivers improves the total antenna gain, and hence, the communication distance. The proposed antenna was measured and compared to a 26dBi horn antenna. The measured gain when the antenna is directly attached to a WR3.4 waveguide is around 21.2dBi.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Rectenna and Rectifying Circuits for Far-Distance Wireless Power Transfer
abstract: This paper describes the design aspects of large-scale millimeter-wave rectenna and fully-integrated rectifiers for far-distance wireless power transfer (WPT). Considering the atmospheric attenuation and size of the rectenna array, W-band becomes popular for far-distance WPT applications. To maximize the efficiency of WPT system, prior-art rectifying circuits are reviewed, including Schottky-diode-based rectifiers and recently proposed CMOS switching rectifying circuits. The limitations of prior-art designs will be discussed and outlook will be given.

articleTitle: A 28GHz, 7mW, 32dB Gain and 3.3dB NF, Gm-Boosted CG-CS LNA for 5G RF Beamformers
abstract: A low power, high gain 28GHz mm-wave two stage cascaded CG-CS LNA in a 45nm bulk CMOS process is reported for low power 5G RF beamformers. High gain in the LNA is essential in RF beamformers to compensate the loss from passive phase shifters unlike a hybrid beamformer. To achieve high gain, low NF and low power consumption, the first stage utilizes the concept of passive gm boosting in a CG cascoded stage coupled with series peaking. A regular CS cascoded 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>stage boosts gain further. Post-layout EM simulations predict a gain of 32dB and a noise figure of 3.3dB at a power consumption of only 7mW. As a proof of concept, a traditional two stage cascoded CS LNA has also been implemented utilizing slow wave transmission lines to highlight a 3X increased power consumption with similar small signal gain and NF. An IC, package and PCB co-analysis methodology for such mmwave blocks is also introduced as it becomes essential to verify the chip in context of Package/PCB before tapeout.

articleTitle: A Doubler-based 300-GHz CMOS Up-Conversion Mixer for Terahertz Communication
abstract: Recently, IEEE standard 802.15.3d has been established for wireless communication in the frequencies from 252 to 321 GHz. It is expected that the high-speed wireless communication can be realized by using such a wide frequency band. We have realized 300-GHz wireless transceivers in CMOS technology. The mixer-first and mixer-last architecture was used for the transceivers because an amplifier cannot be realized in 300-GHz band due to the low unity-power-gain frequency of a MOSFET. Therefore, an up-conversion mixer plays a very important role in a transmitter. We have proposed a doubler-based harmonic mixer called a square mixer suitable for 300-GHz transmitter. In this paper, I discuss the design and performance of the square mixer.

articleTitle: 28 GHz Band Direct RF Undersampling Broadband Receiver for Ka-Band HTS On-Board Unit
abstract: Direct RF undersampling is an effective technique for miniaturization of HTS on-board unit. It can realize a reception bandwidth up to half of the sampling frequency fs/2 theoretically. However, if it expands reception bandwidth until fs/2, roll-off part of an anti-aliasing filter effects seriously on folding noise. In this paper, we propose a new folding noise model for broadband considering a roll-off part of an anti-aliasing filter. Based on the proposed model, 28 GHz band direct RF undersampling broadband receiver is designed and evaluated. As a result, the reception bandwidth is achieved 94% of fs/2.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Imaging Method based on Frequency-Diverse Subarrays
abstract: Method to reconstruct images with frequency diverse subarrays at millimeter-wave frequencies is presented. The imaging system consists of a set of transmit and receive subarrays each having unique, strongly frequency-dependent radiation pattern. Signal transmissions between different transmit and receive subarray pairs are recorded at multitude of frequencies and the image is solved from the set of these measurements. Target space is observed with each subarray pair and with the known subarray field patterns, the target locations are determined. Simulation study of the method has been conducted and the evaluation of the results proves that the method is viable and could be used for imaging purposes.

articleTitle: Design of Broadband Branch-Line Couplers Utilizing Coupled Transmission Lines at Ka-Band
abstract: This paper describes broadband branch-line couplers (BLCs)with arbitrary coupling factors at Ka-band. The coupler has open-/short-circuited coupled transmission lines as external matching networks and a pair of branch-lines. Electromagnetic simulations for designed broadband couplers with coupling factors from -3 dB to -30 dB based on the equivalent admittance approach are carried out to verify the band-broadening design method.

articleTitle: Realizing the E-Wall Concept for Indoor 5G
abstract: The so-called e-wall is a recently introduced concept with the implementation goal of making a flexible and cost-efficient infrastructure for next generation wireless communication systems in indoor environments. This paper discusses the importance of the e-wall concept and presents some initial attempts to realize it.

articleTitle: Development of Microwave Reflectometer for Glucose Content Measurements
abstract: In this paper, a low-cost portable microwave reflectometer is designed and developed to measure glucose content in aqueous solution. The proposed microwave measurement system is constructed by using microwave circuit with a non-invasive open-ended coaxial probe sensor. Reflection method is used due to its simplicity and suitability of detecting the glucose concentration. The reflected microwave signal is detected by coaxial probe sensor and converted into voltage signal using power detector. Empirical models between the reflection coefficient and the glucose concentration from 10% to 60% have been developed. The reflectometer measurements are compared with Vector Network Analyser, and validated using different batch of samples. The proposed reflectometer demonstrates reasonable accuracy with an error of less than 4.5%.

articleTitle: A 40 GHz Linear Driver Amplifier for Optical ATE Using GaN HEMT with InGaN Back Barrier
abstract: With continuously increasing transmission rate, automated test equipment (ATE)will be demanded in optical communication markets. In this paper, we described linear driver amplifier for optical ATE using Gallium Nitride high electron mobility transistor (GaN HEMT)that can be expected to have large output voltage swing and high linearity in high frequency region. The linear driver amplifier employing distributed amplifier configuration shows small-signal gain of 12 dB, -3 dB bandwidth of 44 GHz and output eye amplitude of 8.4 vpp, and clear output eye diagram is observed at 40 Gbaud non-return-to-zero (NRZ)waveform.

articleTitle: Incoherent Active Millimeter-Wave Imaging Using Forward-Illuminating Source
abstract: In this paper, the forward illuminating source is applied to the passive millimeter-wave (PMMW)imaging technique in order to improve contrast between the objects and human body. Imaging data for the cases of several material are compared with changing the geometry of materials. As a result, the relation is clarified between the imaging data and the analytic reflectivity, emissivity and transmittance.

articleTitle: X-Band Near-Field Focusing Leaky-Wave Antenna with Inhomogeneous Waveguide
abstract: We propose the near field focusing leaky-wave antenna using an inhomogeneous rectangular waveguide. The height of broad-wall is inhomogeneous to obtain focusing effect at the arbitrary position. We propose a design method of the inhomogeneous height of broad-wall of rectangular waveguide. Simulation results and measurement results at X-band are obtained to validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design of W-Band SiGe BiCMOS Low Noise Amplifier
abstract: A W-band low noise amplifier is designed based on the 0.13 μm SiGe BiCMOS process. The two-stage fully differential structure consisting of Cascode is used. In order to achieve good input and output matching performance, transformer matching is adopted between the two stages. Electromagnetic simulation is performed using 3D electromagnetic field simulation software. The simulation results show that the input and output matched well in the 90-100 GHz band. At 94 GHz point, the small signal gain is 15.6 dB meanwhile the input 1 dB compression point power is -14 dBm. The noise figure is 6 dB. The chip size is only 0.48mm × 0.19 mm. This low noise amplifier has good microwave characteristic which is suitable for communication, radar, imaging and other fields.

articleTitle: 60 GHz Dual-Polarized 2⨯2 Phased Array Antenna Using Copper Ball Interconnection
abstract: A 60 GHz dual-polarized phased array antenna using copper ball interconnection is proposed. In this structure, two substrates are vertically connected by copper ball. The top substrate is the dual-polarized array antenna and the bottom substrate is the feeding line. In order to achieve high antenna gain, we examined the effect of directivity synthesis of dual polarized array antenna. The simulation result show 10 dBi beam scanning coverage area of 360° in φ and 40-70° in θ. However, only five of the eight fabricated antennas operated due to implementation failure. Thus, the measurement result show that 10 dBi beam coverage area of 360° in φ and 25-60° in θ.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Shielding of Conductive Polymer Combined Fabric
abstract: There are increasing perception and awareness of electromagnetic interference threats to human bodies and devices. Electroconductive fabrics is one of the solution to protect them by covering/overlapping them. In this paper, we have measured the electromagnetic shielding effect of three kinds of conductive polymer combined fabrics in 1-10GHz and 40-60GHz frequency ranges. Woven fabrics made of conductive paper fiber shows the 8-10dB shielding effect over 8GHz microwave and millimeter-wave frequency ranges.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Intra-Wban Channel Capacity for Toe-Hop Millimeter-Wave WBAN
abstract: Wireless body area network (WBAN)using millimeter wave (mmW)is expected to reduce inter-WBAN interference because of large attenuation, however it is necessary to consider the connectivity of the mmW intra-WBAN communication. We have proposed the toe-hop mmW WBAN in the walking pause and measured on-body propagation losses at 60 GHz. In this paper, we evaluate a channel capacity to show the reliability of the proposed method. Monte carlo simulation shows that the proposed method can ensure the channel capacity of 10 Mbit/s with a probability of more than 99.6% in a walking situation.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Antennas for Mobile Devices and Networks
abstract: Beam-steerable millimeter-wave antennas may enable more efficient use of RF energy in line-of-sight propagation paths than the currently used antennas at microwave frequencies. This paper discusses the challenges related to millimeter-wave antennas for mobile devices and networks and reviews possible approaches for realizing beam-steerable antennas for both applications. The presented millimeter-wave mobile device antenna can use shared volume with the microwave antennas without significantly affecting their performance. The presented antenna for mobile networks makes it possible to integrate active electronics on a single PCB with low-loss waveguide feed network and antenna arrays.

articleTitle: 300-GHz Wireless Data Transmission System with Low-Snr CMOS RF Front End
abstract: A 300-GHz wireless data transmission system based on CMOS usually has low-signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR)output because of both a low output power of a transmitter (TX)and high noise figure of a receiver (RX). As a result, high-gain antennas are commonly employed to make transmission distance longer under the condition. Additionally, its ultra-high operation frequency and its wide channel bandwidth make TX noise dominant, which is mainly generated from phase noise. In this paper, a simple level diagram of the low-SNR CMOS RF front end at operating frequency of 300 GHz is described. And, the 300-GHz wireless transmission system based on CMOS, which had a data rate of 24Gbit/s with 16QAM at a distance of 50 centimeters, was demonstrated using 33-dBi hiah-gain antennas.

articleTitle: High Power and High Efficiency GaN Power Amplifiers for Ku/Ka-Bands Wireless Communication Systems
abstract: Satellite communications becomes more interesting because of an increasing number of satellite launches for especially Ku-band very small aperture terminals (VSAT). The fifth generation mobile communications (5G)are also expected to accommodate the forthcoming huge traffic demands by using millimeter-wave. For such wireless communications, the needs for high power and high efficiency in GaN power amplifier (PA)have been more increasing. This paper presents the prototyped results of state--of-the art GaN PA at Ku/Ka-bands.

articleTitle: E-Band Photonic Transmitter Employing High-Power UTC-PD and Broadband Antenna
abstract: This paper presents a photonics-based E-Band (71-86 GHz)compact broadband transmitter module for wireless communications, which includes a high-speed Uni-Traveling Carrier Photodiode (UTC-PD)coupled to a directive broadband planar antenna. The device exhibits stable optoelectronic frequency response with little fluctuations and a peak radiated power of -6 dBm. We demonstrate the performance within a 3 Gbps real-time data transmission wireless link. The presented development enables realization towards the realization of millimetre wave and terahertz photonic phased antenna array.

articleTitle: An 18–28 GHz Power Amplifier with Drain-Distorted Linearizer in 90 Nm CMOS Process
abstract: An 18-28 GHz power amplifier (PA) featuring the characteristic of the in-band frequencies of sweet spots curves of IMD3 is presented. With the linearizer at the drain terminal of the transistor, the sweet spots curves of IMD3 tolerate a wide range of biases and frequencies variations. The performances of Psat, P1dB, peak PAE of the proposed PA at 24 GHz are 21.7 dBm, 18.8 dBm, and 31.6 %, respectively. With the linearizer activated, the third order intermodulation distortion (IMD3)is improved by 27 dB. At frequencies of 18, 24, and 28 GHz with 40 dBc of IMD3, the output powers reach 10.4, 13.3, and 12.5 dBm, respectively. The chip size occupies 0.36 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. To the best of the authors' knowledge, this PA features the widest frequencies of sweet spots curves of IMD3 compared with the previous works. Additionally, this work is the first to address the tolerance of the linearizer against biases by inserting the linearizer into the PA at the drain terminal of the transistor.

articleTitle: Characteristic Impedance Determination Up to THz Frequencies in Light of Causality
abstract: This paper reviews a recently proposed method of determining the characteristic impedance Z0 of planar transmission lines (TLs) up to THz frequencies. Z0 of a low-loss TL is often determined using the measured propagation constant γ through Z0=γ/(G+jωC), assuming that the parallel conductance G = 0 and that the parallel capacitance C is constant. However, if a TL is inhomogeneously filled with multiple dielectrics, its effective dielectric constant is frequency-dependent and C also is frequency-dependent. If so, the assumption G = 0 is inconsistent with causality. The above method can be augmented in a way consistent with causality by using a method of calibration comparison up to 67 GHz and TL modeling. The method is applied to a CMOS TL from 20 MHz to 220 GHz. Well-behaved and plausible estimate of causal Z0 is obtained over the entire measurement frequency range.

articleTitle: A Beam Alignment MIMO Architecture Based on Directional Antenna Radiation
abstract: In this paper, a beam aligned MIMO (BAMIMO) architecture is proposed, based on the directivity nature of the high gain MIMO antenna port at millimeter wave (mmW) band, with a special attention on the pure line-of-sight (LOS) channel. From the computation results of channel capacity gain (CG)and the singular values it can be seen that, by this BAMIMO system, the CG of the MIMO system with directive radiation can approach that of the omnidirective system with sufficiently large port spacing. The most remarkable characteristic of this BAMIMO is that full degrees of freedom and a high CG can still be obtained if port spacing is zero in either side of the communication link in free space channel, which cannot be acquired by the system with omnidirectional radiation.

articleTitle: Comparison of Millimeter-Wave 0–Ω Transmission Lines in 0.18μm CMOS Technology
abstract: 0-Ω transmission lines (0-Ω TLs)used as a decoupling capacitors in the millimeter-wave band are formed by combining metal-insulator-metal capacitors, metal-oxide-metal capacitors, and MOS capacitors in order to generate a large capacitance. However, due to the differences in the configurations of those capacitors, the frequency characteristics of the 0-Ω transmission lines should also be different. In this paper, we reveal the optimal configuration of a 0-Ω transmission line in the millimeter-wave band in 0.18 μm CMOS technology by electromagnetic simulation. The proposed configuration achieves the characteristic impedance of 1 Ω at 60 GHz. Also, it is sufficient to use a length of 78 μm when the 0-Ω transmission line is used at the tip of a short stub at 60 GHz.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Power-Combining Waveguide Antenna for LINC Transmitters
abstract: This paper addresses the design of a dual-polarized power-combining waveguide antenna for LINC transmitters. The proposed antenna has a port isolation of -13 dB, a fractional bandwidth of > 60% and produces a radiation pattern having a beamwidth of 60° at the design frequency of 2.45 GHz. Measurements of LINC performance for a 32 QAM modulated signal yield an EVM of 0.12% and an ACPR of 30 dBc in boresight direction.

articleTitle: Optical Radio Channel Propagation in Wireless Communication Systems with LEDs
abstract: This paper analyzes optical radio channel propagation characteristics by means of experimental measurement. The channel with an LED and a PD provided by the outstanding technologies co. ltd., is defined as an optical radio channel, and its delay profile is measured by NI-USRPs. As a result, small delayed paths are detected due to the LED or the PD in use. The delay profile is evaluated in a system with single carrier modulation where the frequency domain equalization is applied, in terms of the bit error rate (BER). The transmission performance is about 2dB degraded due to the small delayed paths.

articleTitle: Design of On-Board Impedance Matching Circuit for Millimeter-Wave Presystem
abstract: A millimeter-wave presystem is a system whose RF part is composed of a set of RF modules of element circuits connected via waveguides instead of being composed of an MMIC. Introducing the millimeter-wave presystem enables to shorten overall development period because the millimeter-wave presystem can be built at an early stage of MMIC development and therefore the application development can be started earlier by using the presystem. To build the millimeter-wave presystem, on-board impedance matching circuits are essential to suppress return loss in each RF module. This paper describes the design of an on-board impedance matching circuit for 79GHz millimeterwave presystem. To ensure simulation accuracy, the bonding wire, PCB, and IC in the RF module were separately modeled to fit with measured data. The on-board impedance matching circuit was designed by using these models. Owing to these accurate models, the fabricated impedance matching circuit achieved a return loss smaller than -10dB.
